ceiling_directive: Prove a uniform random-objective localization lemma covering the full coefficient range, including order-sqrt(m) baseline–treatment singular-value crossings, and extend it to explicitly rate-bounded approximate orthogonality.
improvement_directive: Replace the asserted tail argument with a rigorous Ky-Fan or joint-subspace proof of global argmin tightness through every singular-value crossing. Then derive the same phase and coverage conclusions under a specified vanishing rate for the four orthogonality errors.
critique: The advertised uniform global selection law is not fully proved: the passage to equation (21) extrapolates the large-spike expansion and asserts a joint Schur-complement bound over coefficients of order sqrt(m) without controlling baseline–treatment singular-value crossings, where the invoked denominators need not remain separated. Because this tightness and global localization step is load-bearing, compact profile convergence alone does not establish the estimator-level absorption iff law or the downstream zero-coverage result. The outlier and singular-vector-overlap lemmas are also left without proofs or theorem-number-level citations matching their exact uniform and projection claims. Even after repairing those gaps, the delivered contribution is an exact-oracle sensitivity result built on four hand-crafted finite-array orthogonalities, with no robustness to approximate or estimable residualization and no applied evidence, which keeps it below field level and constrains the projected journal score. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
